summary: Formatting project documentation professionally — styles, headers and footers by section, footnotes and endnotes, and well-formatted tables.

theory.title: Headers and footers in a long document

blocks.title: Different headers for different chapters
items: Insert a **section break (next page)** before each chapter.
Open the header of the new section and **unlink** it from the previous one ("Link to previous" off).
Type the chapter name in the header; insert a **page-number field** in the footer.
For the title page tick **Different first page** so it has no header or number.
For printed, double-sided documents use **Different odd & even pages** (page numbers on the outside edge).

blocks.title: Fields often used in headers and footers
rows: Today's date or the date of saving
End of the section or document
Short explanations the reader needs immediately
i, ii, iii … by default in Word

blocks.content: Footnotes **renumber automatically** — never type the numbers yourself. To delete a footnote, delete its **reference mark** in the text, not the note at the bottom.

items.title: Structure
items.content: Insert rows/columns, **merge** cells for a title spanning several columns, **split** cells, set column widths (AutoFit to contents/window).

items.title: Appearance
items.content: Table styles, borders, shading of the header row, alignment of text in cells, text direction.

items.title: Long tables
items.content: **Repeat header row** on each page; allow rows to break across pages or not.

items.title: Captions and references
items.content: *Insert Caption* → "Table 1", automatically numbered; a **table of figures** can be generated from captions.

items.title: Data
items.content: Sort rows; simple formulas (=SUM(ABOVE)); convert text to a table and back.

blocks.text: Styles — the basis of good formatting

blocks.title: Direct formatting vs styles
columns: Direct formatting (bold, size changed by hand)
rows: Must be repeated for every heading
Change the style once → every heading changes
Headings feed the **table of contents** and the navigation pane

blocks.title: A professional layout for a project report
blocks.content: Title page (different first page, no header) → table of contents → chapters starting on a new page with **Heading 1** → header with the project name, footer "Page *n* of *N*" → tables with captions and repeated header rows → footnotes for sources → reference list.
